newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex called lower, correction eyed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex called lower, correction eyed.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were called to open 10 to 15 cents lower Monday, while gasoline and heating oil futures were seen 0.25 to 0.50 cents a gallon lower as the market prepared for a correction to Friday's rally, traders said.
"People are a little wary of the market. The impression is that it should go lower," one trader said.
June crude futures closed on Friday at $22.12, up 82 cents on the day. June Gasoline settled at 65.87, up 1.83 cents a gallon, while heating oil gained 1.99 cents to end at 58.47 cents a gallon.
June crude futures expire on Tuesday amid expectations of another heavy physical delivery like last month's, a factor which likely will keep the market volatile, traders said.
But the absence of clear fundamentals and the willingness to take back some of last week's advance had dealers ready for a declining session, although the cash market was seen holding some firmness.
"There's plenty of supply around. There's nothing in the last two weeks" in the way of fundamentals that would account for the rally, a trader said.
"We're just going to be giving back some of Friday's gain," another trader said.
